notes: lab original: 90% VBINX + 10% BTC while BTC's last month-end close > its 10-month SMA (DD-TREND gate), else 100% VBINX; first US trading day of each month, BTC bars dated < today; monthly rebalance to target; bench VBINX; 25bp; factor regression uses weekdays only (weekend sleeve returns excluded there); vault sealed from 2024-11

red_team.summary: The numbers are real: no look-ahead, no calendar trick, no stale-price effect. They hold on ETFs and on GBTC, the only BTC you could buy at Schwab before 2024. But the 15%/yr vs 8%/yr comes from owning 10% Bitcoin through 2014-2024, not from the trend rule. Simply holding a fixed 10% BTC sleeve made the same 15.3%/yr with almost the same Sharpe (1.02 vs 1.07, identical once the rule's warm-up is excluded). The rule's only proven benefit is a smaller worst drop (-24% instead of -28%), and without 2017 the whole result falls below the PASS bar (96% confidence).
red_team.finding: static 10% BTC sleeve does as well (15.3%/yr, Sharpe 1.02; rule-minus-static t -0.16); without 2017 confidence 96.4%; edge = owning BTC, not the trend rule
